title: Book 2, Aphorisms 1–10
author: Francis Bacon
source: *Novum Organum*, Book 2, Aphorisms 1–10, in the English translation edited by Joseph Devey (New York: P. F. Collier & Son, 1902), 108–121. Bacon published the *Novum Organum* in Latin in 1620.
summary: The aim of human knowledge is the discovery of forms, the laws that make a nature what it is, as the aim of power is to superinduce new natures on bodies. Bacon distinguishes the latent process and latent conformation of bodies, divides philosophy into physics and metaphysics, and lays out the plan of the interpretation of nature.
